description:
Filed 2026-08-14 at the maintainer's instruction, alongside op-21rt (the corrector loop is not converged and its test is now ignored).

THE GAP. crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/examples/htgr_sim_v1/physics/steam_generator.rs is the most load-bearing sub-model in the simulator -- measured at ~96% of HtgrPlant::step's compute -- and it has twelve tests, ALL of which are VERIFICATION (is it implemented correctly?). Per VERIFICATION_AND_VALIDATION.md that answers only half the question. There is NO VALIDATION (does it represent physical reality well enough for its purpose?) -- not against a published HTR-10 steam-generator duty/outlet dataset, not against an analytical counter-flow limit, not against a benchmark.

WHAT EXISTS (verification, all passing, do not duplicate):
  counter_flow_index_map_is_its_own_inverse
  the_station_seed_spans_its_two_end_temperatures
  metal_mass_is_derived_from_tube_geometry
  energy_balance_closes_across_the_exchanger
  a_duty_step_is_filtered_by_the_metal_time_constant
  the_cold_stream_resolves_all_three_zones
  the_gui_millisecond_timestep_reaches_the_same_state
  sub_substep_calls_accumulate_rather_than_advancing_or_vanishing
  impossible_configurations_are_rejected
  the_courant_number_bounds_the_array_substep
  the_corrector_substep_trade_is_measured
  saturation_temperature_matches_if97_reference  (the ONE with an external reference, and it validates the STEAM TABLES, not the exchanger)

WHY VALIDATION IS BLOCKED, AND THIS IS THE HONEST PART. docs/reactor-scoping/htr10-plant-data.md line 762 records the entire steam-generator tube geometry -- diameters, wall thicknesses, coil pitch, tube count -- as UNSOURCED, calls it 'the largest open gap', and notes 'the one figure available for it does not survive arithmetic'. So metal_mass_is_derived_from_tube_geometry verifies that the mass follows correctly from geometry that was INVENTED. The arithmetic is checked; the inputs are not sourced. No validation claim is possible until that is fixed.

SUGGESTED ORDER:
1. Source the tube geometry. htr10-plant-data.md suggests 'a dedicated INET steam-generator paper' as the next place to look. Catalogue whatever is found through kovan per the hard rule; decide the access tier from its own copyright page.
2. Add an ANALYTICAL validation that does not need HTR-10 data at all: the nodalised counter-flow exchanger must reproduce the closed-form single-phase counter-flow effectiveness-NTU result in the limit where the cold side stays single-phase and the metal capacity is driven to zero. That is a real validation of the discretisation and is available TODAY, independent of item 1.
3. Only then attempt a plant-level duty/steam-outlet comparison against published HTR-10 operating data.

RELATED: op-21rt (corrector convergence -- the steam outlet is the quantity that moved 29.3 K, so these two may share a cause), op-szmi.6 (invented secondary-loop geometry), op-jyyp.9 (helical-coil once-through SG), op-npc5 (the nodalised SG itself), op-szmi.14 (promoting it into tampines -- do NOT promote an unvalidated model without saying so).

Per the workspace rule, whatever lands must document BOTH methodology and measured results with uncertainty in the test's /// doc comment.
title: htgr_sim_v1 steam generator: V&V -- 12 verification tests, ZERO validation, and the tube geometry is invented

design:
Part of the dwsim-libs maturity epic (bn op-otqe).

Three fresh Haiku agents, each with no prior context, working from **rustdoc,
public examples, the crate prelude and compiler feedback only**. No
implementation inspection during the first attempt; needing to read internals
is itself a friction event to be logged.

Note before starting: **this crate currently has no prelude and one example**,
so the discovery surface an agent is meant to work from barely exists. Expect
that to dominate the first friction log, and consider whether a prelude should
land before or after the first run — there is an argument either way, and the
"before" case loses the measurement of how bad its absence is.

## Task 1 — crude characterization

> Using only rustdoc, public examples, the crate prelude and compiler feedback,
> characterize a representative heavy crude around 22 degAPI. Inspect its bulk
> properties and generate the pseudo-components needed for downstream refinery
> simulation. Do not inspect implementation source during the first attempt.

**A user should not need to understand internal DWSIM module organization
merely to characterize a crude.**

## Task 2 — atmospheric CDU

> Build and solve a steady-state atmospheric crude distillation column for the
> heavy crude using only the public API. Report convergence, stage
> temperatures, overhead, side draws and atmospheric residue. Verify total
> material balance independently.

The obvious workflow should be roughly:

```rust
let crude  = BlackOilCrude::heavy();
let config = CrudeColumnConfig::atmospheric_default();
let result = solve_crude_column(&crude, &config, 12)?;
```

**Do not force this exact shape if the crate has a better existing
abstraction.**

Verify at least: feed flow; all product flows; sum of product flows; stage
temperature profile; iteration count; final solver residual; thermodynamic
package; pressure; reflux ratio; feed stage; side-draw stages.

**Mass and component conservation must be checked independently, not inferred
from solver convergence.** A converged residual says the equations were
satisfied as written; it does not say the equations conserve anything.

## Task 3 — vacuum distillation

See the separate VDU issue — that task is as much an architecture question as a
dogfood, and its outcome may be "not currently expressible", which is a
legitimate and useful result.

## Procedure

Per #63: record friction, do not immediately hand over the correct API, inspect
the log, fix genuine defects, add a public example of the corrected workflow,
then re-run with a **fresh** agent against the fixed API.

**Independently verify every numerical claim.** In #58, four of six agent
reports contained a confident, wrong physics claim. Friction logs were
reliable; physics assertions were not.
title: dwsim-libs: Haiku dogfood runs for crude characterization and atmospheric CDU

description: FINDING 2026-08-11, from implementing the analytic ZBS closure (op-jyyp.3). The 18-point pebble-bed effective-conductivity tabulation in reference-data/virtual_test_bed/htgr/generic-pbr/pbr.i block keff_pebble_bed (300-2000 K, 11.94-44.95 W/(m K)) -- transcribed as the reference table in crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/htr10/zbs.rs and named the acceptance target for the analytic ZBS -- CANNOT be produced by the Zehner-Bauer-Schlunder correlation with the deck's own stated inputs (eps=0.39, d_pebble=0.06 m, emissivity=0.8, graphite k_s=26 W/(m K), helium at 6 MPa). Evidence, all computed 2026-08-11: (1) full ZBS (van Antwerpen 2010 form, contact phi=0.0077, C=1.25) with helium k_f from the KTA 3102.1 correlation gives 2.08 W/(m K) at 300 K vs the table's 11.94 (-83%), 10.5 vs 27.3 at 1000 K, 29.0 vs 45.0 at 2000 K; (2) inverting for the fluid conductivity the table would require gives k_f = 3.8 W/(m K) at 300 K rising past 40 at 1300 K -- no gas has this; (3) physically, stagnant-helium graphite pebble-bed effective conductivity at ambient is order 1-2 W/(m K) (SANA/HTTU-class experiments), so 11.94 at 300 K is not a physical stagnant-bed value under any correlation. The generating configuration is unknown -- SAM is closed-source, and the ANL reports (ANL/NSE-19/46, the NT24-115 SAM thermal-fluids paper, ANL pebble-temperature paper) cite the ZBS model but do not print the evaluation that produced this table. The analytic ZBS in crates/tampines/src/pebble_bed/zbs.rs carries a documented-discrepancy test recording the full 18-point comparison. CONSEQUENCE: the zbs.rs module doc in the digital-twin-engine frames this table as 'the published reference an analytic ZBS implementation must reproduce' -- that framing needs revisiting by the maintainer (that crate is owned by another agent; not edited). The table remains a faithful transcription of what the VTB/SAM model USED; the question is whether it is what ZBS PRODUCES. Options: keep the table as the interim bed conductivity (it is what the VTB transient models ran with), use the analytic ZBS, or obtain the full NEA PBMR-400 spec / SAM documentation to resolve the generating inputs.
title: VTB generic-pbr ZBS 18-point k_eff table cannot be reproduced by the ZBS correlation with helium -- reference data suspect
